Complain as soon as you notice the fault

Food and drink are fresh goods. The time to complain is then considerably shorter than three years. Check the goods straight away and contact the shop immediately. That is why no warranty or three-year claim period is shown. This is guidance, not legal advice.
Food and drink are fresh goods: complain right away. No warranty or three-year claim period is shown.

For the first two years the seller must show that the fault did not exist when you bought the item. After that you must show that it did. A warranty can then be better.
Normal wear is not a fault. The fault must have existed when you received the item.
Fresh goods (food and drink): the time to complain is considerably shorter than three years.
Plants have a three-year right to claim faults like other goods, but you must have cared for the plant according to the care instructions. Cut flowers are fresh goods: choose Food and drink.
You must have cared for the plant according to the care instructions you received. Keep photos showing how the plant looked on delivery. Cut flowers count as fresh goods.

Tips: how to get good help

• Be specific: dates, what is wrong and what you want.
• Ask for a short, factual tone. Threats and long essays do not help.
• Do not give an AI your personal ID number, address or card number.
• AI can be wrong about the law. Check the important parts with the Swedish Consumer Agency or Hallå konsument.
• Always read the answer. Then paste it here with "Paste" and send it from your mail app.
• If the store says no: ask the AI to help you reply, and ask about the National Board for Consumer Disputes (ARN).

Rules that apply (the Swedish Consumer Sales Act, 2022:260): the right to complain lasts three years. A fault that appears within two years is presumed to have existed when I received the item. I must complain within a reasonable time after discovering the fault, and two months is always in time. I can first demand that the fault is fixed by repair or replacement, then a price reduction or cancellation of the purchase.

Write the email so it is clear that I am making a complaint and what I demand. Do not invent details I have not given you. Do not include any personal information about me. Tell me if you are unsure about anything in the law so I can check it with the Swedish Consumer Agency.
